title: Evaluating the Consistency of LLM Evaluators
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. It evaluates the consistency of Large Language Models when used as evaluators, specifically focusing on 'Self-Consistency' (consistency across multiple samples) and 'Inter-scale Consistency' (consistency across different scoring scales like 5-point, 10-point, Likert) on general criteria such as harmlessness, helpfulness, factuality, and conciseness.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion, as this topic is outside its scope. The findings focus on the consistency of LLM evaluators, showing that strong proprietary models are not necessarily the most consistent, and that evaluation consistency is a crucial metric for assessing the reliability of LLM evaluators, independent of their performance on other benchmarks.
